standard.title: Investigate composers' and performers' use of elements across cultures and times
standard.description: investigate and analyse ways that composers and/or performers use the elements of music, compositional devices and/or vocal and instrumental techniques across a range of cultures, times and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored how elements of music are combined across cultures and contexts and evaluated personal responses using music terminology (AC9AMU8E01 — Y7-8). They can describe how structural features create effects. The Y9-10 step shifts from exploration to investigation and analysis — specifically examining how composers/performers use elements to influence emotional response, communicate identity, and respond to social and historical contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate and analyse ways composers and/or performers use elements of music, compositional devices and/or vocal/instrumental techniques across a range of cultures, times and contexts.

nodes.label: Analysing how elements and devices evoke response
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how a composer or performer uses specific elements and compositional devices to structure a work or evoke a particular emotional response.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse one piece in depth — identify at least two specific techniques or devices used and explain how each contributes to a particular emotional response.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how composers and performers use elements and devices to structure compositions and evoke emotional responses — examining instrumentation choices, dynamic manipulation, structural devices, expressive techniques; connecting specific musical choices to their emotional and communicative effects; using Viewpoints to guide analysis.
wider: Compare how two composers from different times or cultures use elements to evoke a similar emotional response — analyse what is similar in their approach and what is culturally or historically specific
Use Viewpoints to ask how technology has changed music styles, composition practices, audiences and the music industry — trace one specific technology's influence on compositional choices
nodes.hinge_reason: The move from 'describing' to 'analysing' — connecting specific musical choices to specific effects with evidence — is the defining cognitive step of Y9-10 Exploring and Responding. Students who describe without analysis cannot access the investigation required by the descriptor, and cannot meet the demands of senior music analytical writing.

response_modes.reason: Build the analysis habit with an explicit evidence-to-claim structure: 'The composer uses [specific technique] at [specific moment] which creates [specific effect] because [musical reasoning].' The move from observation to analytical claim to musical reasoning is the progression to make explicit. Viewpoints questions provide a useful scaffold.

success_criteria: Can identify at least two specific techniques or devices in a piece under analysis
Can explain how each contributes to a specific emotional or communicative effect, with musical reasoning

nodes.label: Music in times of conflict, change and social context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how music is used in times of conflict and social change — analysing what compositional and performative choices carry political, social or historical messages.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate one piece of music connected to a specific historical or social context; analyse at least two compositional choices that carry the work's message.
nodes.typical_width: Compare how people in a range of times, places and contexts have used music in times of conflict and change — examining how specific compositional and performative choices carry political or social messages; investigating why music might be described as 'experimental' in its response to social context; discussing how music influences personal and social identity.
wider: Investigate how music used in two different historical or political conflicts uses similar or different compositional strategies to carry its message — compare the musical choices and their social contexts
Analyse how music influences personal or social identity — use this analysis to inform the creation of a piece designed to communicate a specific social or community message

response_modes.reason: Musical responses to conflict and social change span many different historical and cultural contexts — each adds a new example of how the same musical purpose (communicating protest, grief, solidarity) is realised through different compositional choices. Breadth of examples is what enables genuine analytical comparison.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Music's role in social and political contexts is one of the most compelling entry points for students at Y9-10 — it connects musical analysis to real-world significance and makes the analytical work feel purposeful rather than merely academic.
success_criteria: Can identify the social or historical context of a piece of music and connect it to specific compositional choices
Can analyse how those choices carry the work's social or political message, with musical evidence

nodes.label: Experimental music and sound installations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate why music might be described as 'experimental' and analyse how elements of music are manipulated in sound designs for installations or site-specific artworks.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two reasons why a specific piece of music might be described as experimental; describe how at least one element of music is manipulated in an unusual way.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the concept of experimental music — how composers combine techniques from different cultural or historical contexts, how elements are manipulated in installations or site-specific works, how the space and physical context shape the music; discuss what distinguishes experimental music from conventional practice and what it aims to achieve.
wider: Investigate how a specific experimental composer combines techniques from two or more cultural or historical traditions — describe what personal style emerges and what makes it distinct from each source tradition
Investigate how elements of music are manipulated in a sound installation — analyse how the physical space, listener movement and context shape the musical experience

response_modes.reason: Experimental music challenges students' assumptions about what music is and does. Guided questioning — 'Why do you think this was made this way?', 'What is the composer trying to achieve that conventional approaches could not?', 'What does the space add to the music?' — builds the analytical flexibility to engage with unfamiliar sonic contexts.

success_criteria: Can explain why a piece might be described as experimental with at least two musical reasons
Can describe how at least one element of music is manipulated in an unusual or context-specific way
